title: Space Tech Briefing — September 10, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space cadets and cosmic explorers! It's Thursday, September 10, 2026, and the universe is buzzing with incredible news! I'm your host, ready to launch you into the latest and greatest from beyond our blue marble.

First up, a truly breathtaking new view of our universe! NASA's incredible Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, or TESS, has just unveiled its most comprehensive map of the starry sky. This isn't just any map; it's a colossal mosaic, meticulously stitched together from observations spanning April 2018 all the way to September 2025. Imagine this: 96 sectors of the sky, revealing nearly 6,000 vibrant, colored objects. Each one represents either a confirmed exoplanet or a strong candidate, orbiting distant stars! TESS, launched in 2018, is truly revolutionizing our search for other worlds. What an astonishing achievement from the ultimate exoplanet hunter!

And now, bringing us closer to home, but still reaching for the stars, we have exciting news from the European Space Agency! French astronaut Thomas Pesquet has officially begun his intensive training for his next incredible mission. Set for 2027, Pesquet is slated to take command of the Vast-PAM-1 mission, heading straight to the International Space Station. Get ready to follow his journey as he prepares for another historic command in orbit!

What a lineup of stellar news to kickstart your day! From mapping alien worlds to preparing for new human frontiers, the future of space is brighter than ever. I'm your host, signing off for now. Keep looking up, and join us again tomorrow for more groundbreaking discoveries!
